correctness.rationale: Reindex the Strehl expansion by j=n-k and cancel factorials to obtain the product of binomial(n,2j) and the two central binomial coefficients at j and n-j. Legendre gives central-binomial valuation s_2, and the digit-sum inequality bounds each summand's valuation below by s_2(n). Equality needs carry-free addition j+(n-j) and an odd binomial(n,2j). The first condition says the support of j is a submask of n; Lucas gives the corresponding condition for 2j. Thus the set of allowable bits of j is exactly the set of starts of adjacent 11s. Every submask of that set is allowed, including with overlapping pairs: doubling shifts all bits without collision, and the condition 2j<=n follows automatically. Therefore exactly 2^a_2(n) terms are odd after division and the quotient parity follows. The zero index is included, and the length-L binary avoidance count gives Fib(L+2) with zero or Fib(L+2)-1 without it. Dyadic bounds extend to ordinary density zero. The frozen finite checker was read, not executed.
residual_risks: The result does not give the valuation excess on words containing 11; that is not required for the congruence.
